claim: Defaulting to position 0 is a base rate in GPT-2 small, 58 heads in layers 4 to 9, independent of the first token. On repeated random tokens the five lose it mainly through softmax competition from their high induction-target score, not through a separate off state.
nothing_new_because: Competition accounts for 85 to 98% of the fall, and the card's on-off branch couldn't fail because these heads were selected on that score. Whether late heads read from position 0 is untested and low priority.
surprise: Position 0's residual norm is about 14 times position 25's.

It did not isolate previous-token heads, its statistic is no general detector of them, and it misplaced heads such as 4.11 and left the strongest negative heads unplaced.

claim: On repeated random tokens, excluding position 0, the five's keys read largely inside 4.11's 64-dimensional write space (attention on the right position 0.934 to 0.13 with it removed, 0.67 with it kept alone; random subspaces 0.90 and 0.16), and tokens match themselves through 4.11's VO (0.641 of tokens, chance 0.0005). This does not show a channel specific to 4.11: 4.7 gives 0.20, and the drop tracks key-weight share across 60 heads.
new_questions: Which earlier heads' writes, zeroed only for the five's keys, do most of the damage, ranked over all heads and leaving position 0 alone?
surprise: The dramatic collapse at low rank was position 0's huge norm, not the channel. A bug made the earlier self-match 2% when it is 64%.

claim: On gpt2-medium with repeated random tokens, zeroing best-pairing's five heads costs about 42 points of top-1 repeat accuracy, against at most 0.8 for 24 same-layer sets and 4.3 for attention's top 5. This doesn't show attention misses them: the earliest five heads above 0.5 attention cost about the same, and zeroing also raises text loss by 1.10.
nothing_new_because: Q017, already locked, asks why: whether early heads feed late ones.
surprise: The prediction that layers explain it failed. Each pick alone costs at most 0.9, so the effect is joint.

claim: On one scramble of GPT-2 small, a weights-only key edit took random-token repeat accuracy from 0.987 to 0.011 at text rise 0.013. The rule says beyond deletion, but head-list key edits match it: reducing the same heads' keys to their query-bias term gets 0.002 at 0.022. Wider inputs: repeated stories 0.922 to 0.528, word lists at most 0.015, names mixed.

evidence.row: keys reduced to the query-bias term

nothing_new_because: Whether the edit is better than head-list edits is settled for this model: it isn't. What remains is Alex's call on whether a bigger write test is worth it.
surprise: Twice, Astra wrote a clean edit from weights alone and left text nearly intact, because it kept each head's mean output, while plain zeroing cost 0.85 to 1.07.

claim: One capped run on scrambled GPT-2 medium reached repeat accuracy 0.737 at text rise 0.135, not beyond deletion and worse than a head-list edit on the same heads. Its reading was right: its three sources are the model's three strongest previous-token heads, 4.13, 5.11 and 6.7, and its targets are the same set a simple recipe finds.
new_questions: With a higher budget, does Astra's write on medium improve, or does more turns not help?
surprise: It adapted to several source heads on its own, so reading carried over to the bigger model better than writing did. One run hit its cost cap, so 'doesn't scale' isn't supported.

claim: On GPT-2 medium, silencing the picks only for later heads' queries cuts seven late heads' attention by 40%, and keys by 6%, but costs only 0.6 points of repeating, or 10.3 through all later queries, out of 41.2. So late heads depend on the picks, and that route isn't what carries the damage.
new_questions: On medium, where do the other 30 of the 41 points go: direct effects of the picks on the logits, or their effect on other mid-layer heads?
surprise: The ladder is real but doesn't explain the cost.
